items.title: 19.2 Hydrocarbons (Compounds of Carbon and Hydrogen Only)

blocks.title: Hydrocarbons
blocks.text: Hydrocarbons are compounds that contain carbon and hydrogen only.

items: Open-chain (acyclic) hydrocarbons are usually called aliphatic hydrocarbons (from the Greek aleiphatos, fat, because fats have open-chain structures). They are saturated (alkanes) or unsaturated (alkenes and alkynes).

Closed-chain (cyclic) hydrocarbons contain rings of carbon atoms. Alicyclic hydrocarbons, saturated or unsaturated, behave like aliphatic ones, e.g. cycloalkanes and cycloalkenes. Aromatic hydrocarbons contain a benzene ring or a similar structure, e.g. benzene, naphthalene and diphenylmethane.

blocks.alt: A tree: hydrocarbons (C and H only) split into open-chain aliphatic (saturated alkanes; unsaturated alkenes and alkynes) and closed-chain cyclic (alicyclic and aromatic). Examples below: ethane CH3-CH3, ethene H2C=CH2, ethyne HC-triple-bond-CH; cyclohexane; benzene, methylbenzene and naphthalene.
blocks.caption: Classification of hydrocarbons (original diagram after the book's chart and examples).
blocks.long_description: Hydrocarbons are first divided by their carbon skeleton: open chains (aliphatic) or rings (cyclic). Aliphatic hydrocarbons may be saturated, with only single bonds, or unsaturated, with double or triple bonds. Cyclic hydrocarbons are alicyclic, behaving like aliphatic compounds, or aromatic, containing benzene-type rings.

blocks.prompt: Classify methylcyclohexane, a methylcyclohexene, methylbenzene, naphthalene and cyclohexane as aliphatic, alicyclic or aromatic.
blocks.explanation: Methylcyclohexane, the methylcyclohexene and cyclohexane are alicyclic; methylbenzene and naphthalene are aromatic.

items: Cyclic: alicyclic (e.g. cyclohexane) or aromatic (benzene rings).
